title: Request platooning and KV reservation simplification
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Context: The continuous-batcher scheduler and KV cache reservation logic have accumulated several micro-optimizations and conditional paths implemented over years. This has increased cognitive overhead, caused subtle reservation leaks, and made admission and prefetch behavior difficult to reason about under bursty traffic. The goal of this ticket is to simplify request 'platooning' (grouping of short-lived requests to reduce head-of-line variance), unify the KV reservation API, and remove three legacy fast-paths that complicate lease lifecycles.
progress:
2025-02-28: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and DX (Aisha, Marcus, Elena). Agreed scope: (1) introduce platoon metadata on ingress, (2) replace ad-hoc kv_reserve()/kv_touch() with a single Reservation token object, (3) delete legacy fast-paths fp_read_a/fp_read_b.
2025-03-03: Bench harness (bench/platooning-runner) added; initial synthetic load shows 8-12% reduction in P99 under 95th-percentile burst patterns after platooning simulation.
2025-03-04: Prototype PR opened (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/8421). Early review flagged race in Reservation drop path.
2025-03-05: Added deterministic unit test for reservation double-free and a lightweight instrumentation metric (kv.reservations.drops) to trace regressions.
Next: address code review comments, run canary in dedicated staging (small fleet), and validate on real traffic shadowing for 72 hours.
acceptance_criteria:
- All existing end-to-end test suites pass (unit, integration, long-tail load).
- No increase in kv.reservations.drops in staging vs baseline.
- P95 and P99 generation latency in canary show no regression; target: <= +1% p95, p99 improves by >=5% under bursty micro-bursts.
- No increase in memory usage beyond 3% at steady-state.
- Design doc and README updated; PR approved by two reviewers and merged with feature-flag gated rollout.
- Migration plan executed: staged rollout across zones and automated rollback triggers in Console when kv.reservations.drops > baseline + 3*sigma.
tech_notes:
Design summary: Introduce a 'Platoon' lightweight descriptor attached to ingress requests (max 128 bytes) that hints at grouping boundaries; scheduler will use platoon id to coalesce requests into micro-batches when sequence lengths are small and deadlines align. KV Reservation: Replace free functions with Reservation object implementing RAII semantics (acquire(), extend(), release()). Reservation holds a shard token and target TTL; the runtime reconciler centralizes eviction decision-making to remove lease fragmentation.
Trade-offs: Platooning may add a small scheduling delay (configurable hysteresis 0-6ms) for short-lived requests; we expose this as a per-route knob. The Reservation object increases one pointer indirection per inflight session but dramatically reduces state-machine complexity and test surface.
Backward compatibility: All existing routes default to platoon-enabled=false; we will flip for low-latency candidate routes during canary. Reservation API is internal; no public SDK change required.
Open questions: whether to persist platoon metadata through retries and how to treat prefetch-primed KV entries when a reservation expires mid-batch. We decided to prefer preserving stale KV entries for the remaining batch to avoid churn, and rely on reservation TTL tuning to bound staleness.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: reservation double-free leading to KV entries being evicted prematurely. Mitigation: deterministic unit tests and runtime instrumentation for kv.reservations.drops; abort canary on anomaly.
Risk: slight latency added by platoon hysteresis. Mitigation: expose per-route config and start with lower-traffic routes; track p50/p95/p99 per-route in Console.
Risk: scheduler bug causing starvation of non-platooned requests. Mitigation: ensure fair-queue sampler and priority inversion guard in scheduler; add chaos tests to CI.
